mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to anticipated monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI increases do not correlate with subsequent FEDFUNDS rate hikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases do not correlate with subsequent GDP declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods following two consecutive GDPC1 declines, or GDPC1 declines do not correlate with subsequent earnings revisions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases do not correlate with subsequent earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5%, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 25 basis points in a month signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decreases do not correlate with subsequent equity rallies.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of periods following two consecutive RSAFS increases, or RSAFS increases do not correlate with subsequent consumer discretionary sector outperformance.
